title: Constructing Composite Graphs y = f(g(x)) from Component Graphs
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Use the given graphs of f and g on [-4, 4] to determine the equations and key vertices for sketching the composite graph y = f(g(x)): (a) f is piecewise linear with vertices (-4, 2), (-2, 0), (0, 2), (4, -2), and g is piecewise linear with vertices (-4, -4), (-2, 0), (2, 0), (4, 4); (b) f is piecewise linear with vertices (-4, -4), (-1, 2), (1, 0), (3, 4), and g is a smooth curve passing through (-4, 2), (-2, 0), (0, -2), (1, -2.5), (4, 0).
finalAnswer: \text{(a) Piecewise linear through } (-4, 2), (-3, 0), (-2, 2), (2, 2), (3, 0), (4, -2);\quad \text{(b) Continuous curve passing through } (-4, 1), (-2, 1), (0, -1), (1, -2), (4, 1)

steps.title: Write Piecewise Formulas for f and g in Part (a)
steps.mathExpression: f(u) = \begin{cases} -u - 2, & -4 \le u \le -2 \\ u + 2, & -2 < u \le 0 \\ 2 - u, & 0 < u \le 4 \end{cases}, \qquad g(x) = \begin{cases} 2x + 4, & -4 \le x \le -2 \\ 0, & -2 < x < 2 \\ 2x - 4, & 2 \le x \le 4 \end{cases}
steps.explanation: From the vertices in Figure 22(a), derive the linear equations on each subinterval for both f(u) and g(x).
steps.why: Each straight segment between two vertices (x_1, y_1) and (x_2, y_2) is determined by its slope (y_2 - y_1)/(x_2 - x_1).

steps.title: Trace the Composite Function y = f(g(x)) Across Subintervals in Part (a)
steps.why: Splitting [-4, 4] at points where g(x) crosses the corner inputs u = -2 and u = 0 of f yields the exact piecewise linear vertices of f(g(x)).

steps.title: Evaluate Key Point Mappings (x, g(x)) -> (x, f(g(x))) in Part (b)
steps.mathExpression: \begin{aligned} x = -4 &: g(-4) \approx 2 \implies f(g(-4)) = f(2) = 2 \\ x = -2 &: g(-2) = 0 \implies f(g(-2)) = f(0) = 1 \\ x = 0 &: g(0) = -2 \implies f(g(0)) = f(-2) = 0 \\ x = 1 &: g(1) \approx -2.5 \implies f(g(1)) = f(-2.5) = -1 \\ x = 4 &: g(4) = 0 \implies f(g(4)) = f(0) = 1 \end{aligned}
steps.explanation: In Figure 22(b), f has slope 2 on [-4, -1] (so f(u) = 2u + 4), slope -1 on [-1, 1] (so f(u) = 1 - u), and slope 2 on [1, 3] (so f(u) = 2u - 2). Tracking g(x) at x = -4, -2, 0, 1, 4 and reading f at those heights gives the composite curve.
steps.why: Pointwise composition plots (x, f(g(x))) by using the vertical height g(x) on the first curve as the horizontal input to f.
